comparison: Perfect alignment on nsy-1 genetic findings (C14-C22). Both evaluations find the forward genetic screen, allele confirmation, behavioral defects, and survival costs strongly support nsy-1's role in SS detection. OpenEval provides detailed experimental breakdown while peer review emphasizes the genetic screening approach's strength.

Complete agreement on AWC-specific function of NSY-1 (C26-C30). Both evaluations support the tissue-specific localization through expression patterns, rescue experiments, and knockout studies. OpenEval highlights convergence of gain/loss-of-function data; peer review confirms mechanistic identification without concerns.

Full concordance on AWC neuron state regulation (C31-C46). Both evaluations accept the str-2::GFP reporter data, genetic epistasis, and AWC ablation experiments. OpenEval emphasizes the critical functional validation from ablation; peer review summarizes the ON-OFF state mechanism as significantly improved.

Strong agreement on STR-130 pathway findings (C47-C66). Both evaluations support the transcriptomics, RNAi screening, and epistasis analysis establishing STR-130 as NSY-1-dependent regulator. OpenEval details the linear pathway evidence; peer review specifically praises the RNA-seq analysis and positive/negative data mining strategy.

Complete alignment on PMK-1 pathway independence (C82-C87). Both evaluations accept that PMK-1 and INS-23 represent separate pathways based on lack of epistasis. OpenEval provides experimental detail on pmk-1 knockdown; peer review accepts the pathway distinction as part of the convincing mechanistic framework.

Strong concordance on overall mechanistic model (C103-C119, with peer review missing C117). Both evaluations support the integrated neuron-gut communication system. OpenEval synthesizes the pathway from neuronal sensing through insulin signaling to intestinal regulation; peer review emphasizes the food quality control system and physiological adaptation mechanism.

High agreement on INS-23/DAF-2 pathway (C67-C79 in OpenEval; C67-C81 in peer review). Both evaluations support the transcriptomics, RNAi screening, and epistasis data. OpenEval focuses on ins-23 induction and DAF-2 promotion of digestion; peer review highlights RNA-seq revealing distinct regulatory pathways and identifies INS-23/DAF-2 as critical signaling factors.

Strong alignment on SS detection and protective shutdown (C1, C3-C8, C12-C13 shared; peer review includes C10-C11). Both evaluations support behavioral avoidance, developmental arrest, and survival data. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple assays; peer review notes all three reviewers affirm conclusions without concerns and cites solid/convincing evidence.

Strong concordance on BCF-1 neuron-to-intestine signaling (C91-C102). Both evaluations support the reporter assays, genetic epistasis, and tissue-specific RNAi demonstrating NSY-1 inhibits BCF-1 and INS-23 mediates activation. OpenEval details the experimental evidence; peer review confirms BCF-1's role in digestive shutdown via the neuron-intestine pathway.

Partial overlap on digestive activation overcoming growth arrest (C9-C11 in OpenEval; C10-C11 shared with peer R1). OpenEval supports these claims through prior work and developmental experiments. Peer review includes these claims within broader behavioral/developmental phenotype evaluation, affirming without specific critique.

Minimal overlap on tissue-specific DAF-2 function (C80-C81). OpenEval evaluates intestinal DAF-2 rescue experiments showing partial suppression, indicating alternative pathways. Peer review R6 includes these claims within broader INS-23/DAF-2 evaluation, accepting findings without specific concerns about the partial rescue phenotype.

OpenEval marks C118 (speculation about multiple signaling molecules) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses this speculative claim, suggesting peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate or comment on this hypothesis.

OpenEval marks C120-C121 (extrapolation to other organisms) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative hypotheses without comparative data. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these evolutionary/comparative claims, indicating peer reviewers did not explicitly critique or validate these broader implications.
